name: Cherry Blossom
description: Cherry brandy and cognac cut with curaçao and lemon. Japan's own contribution to the Savoy era, built to look like the flower it is named for.
funFact: It was created by Tasaburo Tao at Bar Paris in Yokohama, the port city where Japanese cocktail culture actually began — the same city that produced the Bamboo a generation earlier.

steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard for about 12 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish and serve.

name: Yokohama
description: Gin and vodka under orange and grenadine, with one dash of absinthe doing all the talking.
funFact: A single dash of absinthe carries a drink that is otherwise mostly orange juice — which is why the recipe survives in the old books exactly as written, with the absinthe measured in dashes rather than fractions.

steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard for about 12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Serve without garnish.

name: Joy Division
description: A Martini given Cointreau and three dashes of absinthe. Bright, herbaceous and considerably less austere than the name suggests.
funFact: Phil Ward built it at Death & Co in 2008 by taking a 2:1 gin Martini and adding half an ounce of Cointreau — a reminder that most modern classics are an existing drink plus one idea.

steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir for about 25 seconds until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express a lemon twist over the surface and drop it in.

name: Paper Tiger
description: A Negroni that swapped gin for spiced dark rum. Same bitter architecture, warmer floor.
funFact: It holds the Negroni's equal-thirds structure exactly and changes only the base — the cleanest way to prove that the Negroni is a template rather than a recipe.

ingredients.amount: cubed, plus a large cube to serve

steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir for about 25 seconds.
Strain over a large cube in a rocks glass.
Express an orange peel over the top and drop it in.

name: Brainstorm
description: Irish whiskey with a quarter-ounce each of dry vermouth and Bénédictine. Small, dry and pre-Prohibition.
funFact: It is one of the few pre-Prohibition cocktails built on Irish whiskey rather than rye — a category that all but vanished from American bars for most of the twentieth century and only came back in this one.

steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir for about 25 seconds until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express an orange twist over the surface and drop it in.

name: Fog Horn
description: Gin, lime and ginger beer over ice. A Moscow Mule that predates the Moscow Mule and never needed a copper mug.
funFact: The Waldorf Astoria put it on the map decades before vodka arrived in America — the gin-and-ginger build the Moscow Mule would later borrow wholesale.

steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add the gin and lime juice.
Top with ginger beer and stir once, gently, to combine.
Garnish and serve with a straw.

name: Blue Train
description: Gin, lemon and curaçao, named for the overnight sleeper to the Riviera. The blue arrived later than the drink did.
funFact: The original was a plain gin-lemon-triple sec sour; the blue curaçao was added decades later so the drink would match the name of the Calais–Mediterranée express it honoured.

steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard for about 12 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Flame an orange peel over the surface if you have one.

name: Prince Edward
description: Scotch and Drambuie held together by Lillet Blanc. A Bobby Burns that traded its vermouth for something lighter.
funFact: It is a Bobby Burns with Kina Lillet where the Italian vermouth should be — the same substitution that made the Vesper and the Corpse Reviver No. 2 taste the way they originally did, before Kina Lillet was reformulated in 1986.

steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir until cold and properly diluted, about 25 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express an orange twist over the top and drop it in.
